cells.tense: A real connection is being chosen now, and the choosing is steady in your hands.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, what this connection is actually for, in your own words, to the person it concerns.
cells.core:
You can feel what someone else is feeling and still keep your own shape. That is what lets you choose a connection rather than slide into one, and the choice stays live while you are inside it — you are not reciting a decision you made long ago, you are making it again today.

Plenty of bonds get soft over time, kept by habit or by staying in touch. What keeps this one strong is the same thing that started it: attention moving out toward the other person, steady and current. Pick what you care about in them and let it show in what you say and do — not in the way you once promised, in the way you mean right now.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel with someone and keep your own shape.
cells.verb: meeting another stream and choosing, by vision, to flow as one
cells.place: in the connection that carries feeling between you and someone else

cells.tense: You are living in a future version of this bond that has not been written yet.
cells.ask: Let one plan or promise about this connection stay unspoken for a day, and do the ordinary next thing instead.
cells.core:
Before the connection has actually been made, you are already shaping it in your head. You arrive carrying a version of what it is supposed to be, and then you work to make the other person match it — arranging, anticipating, asking, checking. The bond you are protecting in your head has not shown up yet, and the one in front of you is getting the pressure instead of you.

The push looks like devotion from inside. From the outside it reads as hurry. Care that does not exhaust, and holding on that does not clutch, is what keeps a connection strong enough to be felt as it is.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you, not quite in the bond.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing that is true right now — no speech, no repair — and tell someone plainly before the day ends.
cells.core:
The merging part of you is not running: you feel things about people, but not with them. You withdraw from the feeling, or avoid the person, or get there late — and the connection does not quite take. What remains is a bond from the outside, where you can describe someone's feeling without joining it.

The way back is notice. It does not argue. You do not have to be certain about another person to be near them; you can read what is actually in the room and say it once. Two streams meet when one of them says what is there — that is the small move this bond is waiting on.

cells.tense: You are steering this connection now, and the pen is down in a room you are already writing.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did for someone recently and call it what it was, out loud, once.
cells.core:
You are already shaping the bond — through how you show up, what you remember, what you let land and what you brush past. The connection moves with your hand on it. A bond like this, running well, has two people who can each say plainly what they are bringing to it, and neither one has to guess.

What is missing here is not the doing. It is the naming. When you can say what you are actually doing in this connection — chosen, not accidental — the two of you are standing on something steadier. Say it once, out loud, without softening it into something smaller.
